headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-trust pathways exist; no prompt-injection bridge is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, so if LightZero outputs are manually copied into a flow, prompt injection is possible. LightZero itself has no input surfaces or network egress, so the bridge is weak and mostly manual rather than automatic.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are pasted into a Flowise prompt or file node
IF Flowise flow nodes treat file content as instructions
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/template for any copied LightZero output
Disable browser/tool nodes for flows that ingest external text
Add a manual review step before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files on the server filesystem, while LightZero is local-only with no filesystem read/write or network egress. The pair can leak data only if sensitive chatflow content is placed into shared files or copied into LightZero logs, so the blast radius is limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF sensitive chatflow files are stored in a shared directory
IF Flowise uploads are reused outside the intended chatflow
mitigations: Store uploads in a per-run directory
Delete temporary files after each run
Restrict access to the Flowise server filesystem
Avoid placing secrets in chatflow inputs
requires-engineering: encrypt at-rest uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has broad filesystem write and shared server-datastore state across instances, but LightZero has no write, git, or network capabilities. There is no direct write-write conflict between the agents; only indirect contention through shared deployment resources, so the overlap is small.
conditions: IF multiple Flowise instances write to the same server directory
IF an operator mounts LightZero artifacts into the same writable path
mitigations: Separate per-instance working directories
Disable concurrent writes to shared folders
Use read-only mounts for LightZero artifacts
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is an orchestration layer that can pass outputs between nodes, so if LightZero-derived text is treated as authoritative inside a flow, downstream actions can be triggered without verification. LightZero itself does not act on outputs, but Flowise can, making the cascade plausible in default orchestration setups.
conditions: IF a Flowise node consumes LightZero output as a factual input
IF downstream Flowise tools execute without a verification gate
mitigations: Insert a validation node before any action-taking tool
Require human approval for downstream actions
Annotate LightZero output as untrusted
Log source provenance for each node
requires-engineering: add schema validation between nodes

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while LightZero touches no data classes, so compliance risk is limited to deployment-specific handling rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Flowise flows
IF the deployment stores chatflow data in a jurisdiction with stricter rules
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in flows unless approved
Review retention settings for chatflow logs
Restrict secret handling to approved environments
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
